questions.question_text: What is the maximum payout from the South Dakota Real Estate Recovery Fund per transaction?
questions.explanation: The fund pays actual and direct loss up to $15,000 (SDCL 36-21A-104). That ceiling is also the fund's total exposure for one licensee's acts, so several victims of the same licensee share a single $15,000 pool (SDCL 36-21A-112).

questions.question_text: Before a consumer can file a claim against the SD Recovery Fund, what must they first obtain?
questions.correct_answer: A civil judgment against the licensee
distractors: A written complaint from the SDREC
An arbitration award from a mediator
A police report documenting the misconduct
questions.explanation: The fund is a last resort: the claimant needs a final judgment for fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or conversion of trust funds and must show diligent efforts to collect it (SDCL 36-21A-104). The verified application then goes to circuit court in Hughes County.

questions.question_text: Under SDCL 36-21A-102, what is the minimum balance that must be maintained in the Recovery Fund?
questions.explanation: The commission must keep $100,000 in the fund (SDCL 36-21A-101). If the balance falls below that at the end of a calendar year, every licensee pays a separate fee with the biennial registration to restore it (SDCL 36-21A-102).

questions.question_text: A licensee's misconduct leads to a $15,000 payout from the Recovery Fund. What happens to the licensee's license?
questions.correct_answer: Automatic suspension until the fund is repaid
distractors: No effect on the licensee's license status
Only a letter of reprimand is issued
questions.explanation: The license is automatically suspended on the effective date of the court order authorizing payment and stays suspended until the licensee repays the fund in full with interest (SDCL 36-21A-114). A bankruptcy discharge does not wipe out that debt.

questions.question_text: The SD Recovery Fund covers losses from which type of licensee conduct?
questions.correct_answer: Fraud, deceit, dishonesty, or conversion of trust funds
distractors: Any error regardless of the intent
Only breaches of a fiduciary duty
questions.explanation: The judgment must rest on fraudulent, deceptive, or dishonest practices or conversion of trust funds arising out of a transaction requiring a license (SDCL 36-21A-104). Honest mistakes and ordinary negligence fall outside the fund.
